_doc: PRE-REGISTRATION for qal/burst -- the wake->calibrate->burst->park duty-cycle composition, QAL banktank vs clock-gated CMOS, written BEFORE the first deck of this workflow ran (directory contained only this file at the recorded mtime). Everything below is stated from the committed record; labels MEASURED / DERIVED / ASSUMED are used as in the campaign.
question: Energy per useful operation as a function of duty (duty = burst time / cycle time), QAL banktank arrangement vs clock-gated CMOS done well, and the crossover duty below which QAL wins. The QAL side is MEASURED end-to-end on a real deck (park -> wake -> burst of >=20 value-checked beats -> park); the CMOS side is MODELLED from measured pieces with every term's provenance named, measured on the same cells where the record lacks a number.

fixture.qal: committed qal/banktank arrangement VERBATIM (bt.py deck emitter reused): 4 restoring inverter banks x 8 cells (1.12u/0.74u, CL=2fF), per-bank tank m=10 (C_tank=359.79 fF), L=15 nH, RS=10, tg15p triple (10u nMOS / 20u pMOS / 2u tank-referenced park, A6), VGH=1.5 V, dV=1.65 V, T=150 ps, H=4 -- the committed PASSing dv1650 row (row_m10_T150_H4_dv1650_free.json). Beat = one bank-hop = 8 gate evaluations.
fixture.burst: 5 waves x 4 banks = 20 beats = 160 gate-ops per burst event. Initiation interval 800 ps (return [c+600, c+~750] must complete before the next rise; the committed II=H*T quote collides return with re-rise on the same switch, so II = 5T+50 -- DECLARED schedule deviation). Input pattern alternates P / ~P per wave so every gate computes a NEW value every wave (this books the CMOS comparator at alpha=1 per op -- its most expensive comb booking; alpha=0.5 reported as a variant). Inputs flip 40 ps before each new wave's bank-1 rise, while bank 1's rail is down.
fixture.zeros: committed zeros_m10_dv1650.json for P-waves; for inverted (~P) waves the odd/even electrical classes swap, so zeros are reused as [z2,z3,z2,z3] (DERIVED reuse, guarded by the measured |I(L)| at every commanded open, reported per wave; the committed dv1650 row itself reads 1.2-1.8 uA against the 1 uA strict gate, so the strict A6 gate is REPORTED, not used as a kill).

park_state: tanks charged (pre-charge V_t0=0.9075 V rule for the head of a burst; post-burst parks hold whatever the burst left), transfer TG off (gt=0, gtp=VGH), park device ON clamping sw to tnk, rails and outputs drained, bank-1 inputs held DC. ASSUMED OFF during park and why the architecture permits it: the pulse-width timer and SAR logic are power-gated (calibrate-on-wake re-establishes timing -- that is exactly what the committed SAR record's calibrate-on-wake mode is for); the VGH/VHI/gtp DC rails are HELD (their park-window draw is metered, expected gate-leakage-class).

expectations.E1_burst_energy_metered: tank energy lost per bank per wave at dv1650 ~38-47 fJ (committed row: 38.7-43.1 fJ to end) => burst metered-only ~0.75-1.0 pJ per 20-beat burst (~4.7-6.3 fJ/gate-op), plus small drive/VHI bookings. DERIVED from the committed single-wave row; waves 2-5 are the unmeasured part (multi-wave operation has never been simulated on banktank).
expectations.E2_burst_energy_complete: with the committed timer tax (302.8 fJ/bank/hop MEASURED in qal/timer) the complete-ledger burst is ~6.1 pJ heavier: ~7 pJ per burst (~43 fJ/gate-op).
expectations.E3_idle_drain: the parked-tank drain is the composition never measured. Candidate paths: OFF transfer TG subthreshold (30 um total width across Vds~0.9 V) vs the tank-cap-node class (committed strip rate 0.575 pA on a 2 fF node). PRE-STATED BAND: P_idle_QAL in [10 pW, 10 nW] for the 4-bank chain; central expectation 0.1-2 nW DOMINATED BY THE OFF TG, i.e. I expect the '1e-5 %/beat' committed tank-node figure to UNDERSTATE the parked drain because the tank sits behind 30 um of off switch, not behind a 2 fF logic node. If the measured drain lands at the tank-node class (~2 pW) instead, that refutes my stated mechanism and the idle term is essentially free as the brief's synthesis assumed.
expectations.E4_wake: one SAR calibrate-on-wake event, committed: 1.5 pJ design point, band [0.7, 4.0] pJ (DERIVED from measured trial-hop + comparator-ceiling numbers; not re-measured here). Amortised over this run's 160-op burst it is ~9.4 fJ/op -- NOT negligible at 20 beats (the committed <0.03 fJ amortisation assumed >=1e4-hop bursts). This run's bursts are deliberately short; the burst-length scaling is reported analytically.
expectations.E5_cmos_burst: comb ~5-8 fJ/gate-op measured on the same 32 cells at 1.2 V; flop terms per active cycle from the committed anchors: floor+tree 28.2 (add8 anchor) .. 70.7 (Vortex placed-CTS anchor, corrected) fJ/flop/cyc, data ~45-64 fJ/flop at alpha_ff=1; with an 8-flop output rank the CMOS burst is ~3-5 pJ per 5-cycle burst (~20-32 fJ/gate-op).
expectations.E6_cmos_idle: clock-gate-only (logic powered): 32 cells x 117-131.5 pW + 8 DFF x 526.5 pW ~ 8 nW (comb term re-MEASURED here on the same cells; DFF cited). Power-gate+SRAM (the committed selection-rule opponent): header off-leak (MEASURED here on a 30 um pMOS header) + 12.09 pW/bit x state bits; retained state is identical on both sides and cancels -- expected ~0.01-1 nW.

pre_stated_crossover.vs_clock_gate_only: QAL (complete ledger) loses at duty ~1 (burst+wake ~8.4 pJ vs ~5 pJ) and WINS below a crossover duty ~1e-5 (band 1e-6..1e-3) where the CMOS idle-leak excess (~6 nW) repays the ~3.4 pJ burst+wake deficit. On the metered-only QAL ledger the burst itself wins and QAL wins at EVERY duty vs this opponent.
pre_stated_crossover.vs_power_gate_sram: THE HONEST HEADLINE OPPONENT. If P_idle_QAL >= P_idle_CMOS (my central expectation, OFF-TG-dominated), then on the complete QAL ledger there is NO crossover -- gated CMOS wins at every duty and the last open regime CLOSES. On the metered-only ledger QAL wins at high duty and the crossover (below which CMOS wins) sits where QAL's idle excess + 1.5 pJ wake eats the ~2.6 pJ burst advantage: T_idle* ~ 2.6 pJ / dP; duty* depends on dP which spans the E3 band -- I pre-state only the SHAPE and that the sign of dP = P_idleQAL - P_idleCMOS decides existence.
pre_stated_crossover.single_most_likely_outcome: gated-CMOS-done-well (power-gate+SRAM, free re-gate) wins at every duty on the complete QAL ledger; QAL's only surviving window is the metered-only lower bound at duty near 1 -- i.e. the bursty regime does NOT rescue QAL at SG13G2, and the campaign's energy story closes.

acceptance.A1_instrument: the committed banktank dv1650 row deck, regenerated byte-identical and re-run in this workflow's own cache, must reproduce >=10 committed .mt0 keys at rel <= 1e-6 (worst key reported); FAIL kills the run.
acceptance.A2_idle_books: the park drain must be PROVEN from meters, not asserted: (a) every energy source in the parked deck carries an integrator and the park-window ledger closes: sum of source draws = tank dE + metered dissipation to within 10% or 0.5 fJ, whichever is larger; (b) a floating 359.79 fF null cap in the same deck must show |dV| <= 1% of the parked tank's |dV| over the same window (solver-drift control, the strip A3 discipline); (c) the drain RATE from two window lengths (>=2x apart) must agree within a factor of 2 (linearity -- licenses the analytic extension); (d) the idle term of the cycle decks must match the dedicated park deck's rate within 2x.
acceptance.A3_burst_correctness: value check (committed pull-down <=0.10 rail / pull-up >=0.50 rail convention) at every bank's boundary instant, EVERY wave: 32/32 x 5 waves on the T_pre=2ns cycle deck; the first post-park wave is the headline correctness datum. Waves 2-5 failing is a REPORTABLE FINDING (multi-wave banktank has never been run), not a silent excuse.
acceptance.A4_composition: QAL cycle energy at >=3 T_idle values decomposes as idle+wake+burst with the idle term linear in T_idle (R^2 >= 0.9 across the 3 points after subtracting the fixed terms).
acceptance.A5_cmos_provenance: every CMOS term carries MEASURED-here / MEASURED-committed / DERIVED / ASSUMED, and the two generosity rules are applied and stated: un-gate/re-gate FREE, wake FREE.
acceptance.A6_sensitivity: curves recomputed with (i) QAL idle books at 10x the measured drain (junction-zeroed lower-bound caveat made real) and (ii) CMOS clock gating half effective, defined as: half of the clock energy (flop floor + tree) that ideal gating removes during idle cycles remains, at the CMOS clock rate. Both reported; the headline crossover quotes the central case with the sensitivity band.

method_notes.long_idle: simulated park is 1-4 ns inside the cycle decks plus a dedicated >=20 ns park-rate deck with relaxed max-step (justified: no fast transient present; its own null control gates it); T_idle beyond the simulated window is extended ANALYTICALLY as P_idle * T_idle using the measured rate -- stated wherever used.
method_notes.metering: 1F-integrator with t0-reference and PRECISION high, or INTEG-I(Vsrc); tank dE convention-free from 0.5*C*(V0^2-V1^2) on the known linear cap; vt/gmin untouched; own PYMS_VAE_CACHE (vae_cache_burst, warmed by COPY from the session's existing banktank cache, never by concurrent build); all decks in qal/burst/; <=4 concurrent heavy jobs.
method_notes.leakage_caveat: sg13lv_compat.sp declares and DISCARDS ad/as/pd/ps -- junction leakage ABSENT, every idle number a LOWER BOUND; carried on every idle figure and made concrete by the 10x sensitivity case.
method_notes.cmos_rail: CMOS comparator runs at its liberty nominal 1.2 V (the committed comparator convention), QAL at dV=1.65; this is the committed cross-style convention, stated, not hidden.
method_notes.ops_per_metered_cycle: both sides are booked per GATE-EVALUATION on the same alternating-pattern computation (the cipher harness-convention trap is closed by construction: one input flip per wave on both sides, 32 evals per wave both sides).
